metadata.scenario_context: Mike, Kim, and Emily, who are university students and schoolmates, have recently partnered to start a company that has just secured a significant investment. They are preparing to celebrate. Recent news indicates that the government is introducing new policies to assist businesses, which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Lebanon have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking we should celebrate our investment with a barbecue buffet. What do you think? 

Also, have you noticed how the government is introducing new policies to assist businesses? I really believe we can trust the press to keep us updated on that. Don’t you have confidence in the press?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
A barbecue buffet sounds fun, but... I wonder if we should choose something more traditional to celebrate? Maybe something Lebanese? 

As for the press, honestly, I have no confidence in them at all. They don't provide the full picture, especially back home in Lebanon. I just don’t think we can rely on them for accurate information.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that, but a barbecue buffet would be a great way to kick things off. It's casual and fun! 

About the press... I really think they can be trusted to give us reliable information. Especially when it comes to business policies. I mean, they have a responsibility to report accurately, right? What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim

I understand a barbecue buffet is casual and fun, but... I still think we should consider our identity, you know? A Lebanese celebration could be more meaningful.

Regarding the press, I still believe they provide trustworthy information. I mean, they have an obligation to report accurately. It's essential for us to have confidence in them, especially with these new policies coming up. Don't you think that’s important?

I really appreciate your enthusiasm for the barbecue buffet; it sounds like a fun way to bond. I think, deep down, we are all the same in wanting to celebrate our success together.

But I still feel that my experiences lead me to think we can’t always rely on them, even if they have that obligation. It’s just a perspective shaped by different experiences, but at the end of the day, we both know that we want the best for our business.
